title: Dual Remission in Patients with Severe Asthma and CRSwNP Treated with Dupilumab: A 24-Month Real-World Study
content: Background: "Remission" is a primary therapeutic goal in severe asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), though definitions vary regarding olfactory function. We evaluated "Dual Remission" kinetics in patients treated with dupilumab over 24 months. Methods: This single-center retrospective study analyzed 28 patients with comorbid severe asthma and CRSwNP. Dual Remission was defined as simultaneous asthma remission (ACT ≥ 20, no exacerbations, no OCS) and CRSwNP remission (SNOT-22 <  40, NPS ≤ 1). We additionally analyzed "Complete Recovery" by applying a stricter composite definition requiring the restoration of normosmia (Sniffin’ Sticks score ≥ 12). Results: At baseline, patients exhibited uncontrolled disease (median ACT 19, NPS 6). Treatment led to rapid asthma remission (85.7% at 12 months, 100% at 24 months). CRSwNP remission was slower but progressive, rising from 57% at 12 months to 88% at 24 months, demonstrating a significant "catch-up" phenomenon. Consequently, Dual Remission rates increased from 54% to 88% by month 24. However, when requiring normosmia for "Complete Recovery," only 32% met the criteria, revealing that 56% achieved clinical silence yet remained hyposmic. Conclusion: Dupilumab is highly effective, enabling 88% of patients to achieve Dual Remission after 24 months. However, full olfactory restitution is distinct from structural polyp regression and harder to achieve, likely due to persistent neuroepithelial damage.
